takeaway: Low aldosterone (Addison disease) causes sodium loss, low blood pressure, potassium retention and acidosis; increased urinary potassium loss is the exception.

question.text: Mineralocorticoid deficiency can cause the following conditions except:

lines.text: Aldosterone comes from the zona glomerulosa, and is lost when the adrenal cortex is destroyed, as in Addison disease.
Without it the kidney loses sodium, and water follows.
Blood pressure falls, giving postural hypotension.
Buccal pigmentation is also a feature of Addison disease.
Aldosterone normally makes the kidney excrete potassium, so in deficiency potassium is retained, not lost.
Retained potassium and hydrogen ions bring metabolic acidosis.
So increased potassium loss is the exception. The answer is B.
